$comment: HOW LONG A LOCAL TOOL MAY TAKE, in milliseconds. Not model calls — those are bounded by the seam's declared timeoutSecs.
$why: Thirteen of these were literals across seven libraries (5000, 10000, 15000, 20000, 30000, 60000, 180000). Each was an independent decision with no single home: a codeline big enough to need longer got a truncated answer from whichever tool hit its cap first, the caller could not tell a timeout from an empty result, and raising one meant finding all of them.
$naming: Named for the WORK, not the caller, so two callers doing the same work share one answer.

tools.$gitReadWhy: Reading state from a git repository — log, status, rev-parse. Local and fast; a repo slow enough to exceed this is worth reporting rather than waiting on.
tools.$codegraphProbeWhy: Checking whether the codegraph binary exists at all. A presence check that takes seconds is a broken PATH, not a slow tool.
tools.$codegraphQueryWhy: One codegraph query against an existing index.
tools.$codegraphExploreWhy: A broader codegraph traversal returning several files.
tools.$codegraphIndexWhy: Building the index over a whole codeline — the one genuinely long local operation here, and the reason a single shared timeout would not do.
tools.$sembleWhy: A semantic search pass over an indexed codeline.
tools.$promptRenderWhy: Rendering a prompt through the template layer in a child process.
tools.$seamResolveWhy: Resolving a seam's invocation environment in a child process.
tools.$localToolWhy: Anything else local and short — the ecosystem scan, a small helper script.
